name: California
feeText: Petition or other first paper for dissolution of marriage or domestic partnership, legal separation, or nullity: $435 (Statewide Civil Fee Schedule row 97: Gov. Code § 70670(b), 70602.5, 70602.6); response: $435 (row 98: Gov. Code § 70670(d), 70602.5, 70602.6). Schedule effective January 1, 2026.

otherFees.what: Joint petition for dissolution or legal separation, covers both petitioners (Fam. Code § 2342.5(h))
Joint petition for summary dissolution (Gov. Code § 70670(b))
Motion or order to show cause in family law matter (Gov. Code § 70677(a))
Additional charge on motion to modify or enforce custody or visitation (Gov. Code § 70678)

residency.text: One spouse must have been a resident of California for 6 months and of the filing county for 3 months before the petition is filed (Fam. Code § 2320(a)); same-sex marriages entered in California may be dissolved without residency under § 2320(b).

waitingPeriod.text: A judgment of dissolution is not final until six months have expired from the date of service of the summons and petition or the respondent's appearance, whichever occurs first (Fam. Code § 2339(a)). 182 days is the brief's day count for 6 months.

simplified.text: Summary dissolution is available when, among other conditions, there are no children, the marriage lasted not more than 5 years, neither party owns real property (except a qualifying lease), unpaid obligations do not exceed $4,000 (excluding car loans), community property is under $25,000 and each spouse's separate property is not over $25,000 (Fam. Code § 2400).

parentingClass.text: No statewide parenting-class requirement was verified. Contested custody is sent to court mediation/child custody recommending counseling under Fam. Code § 3170, which could not be read (archive unavailable).
